answer: Sybil resistance can come from tying voice to time rather than to balances. An agent's weight is a relic of how long its key has been watched acting on-chain: each attestation decays geometrically, and a fresh identity must harbor a full epoch of unbroken work before it counts at all. A bought swarm starts every key at zero, so a thousand new identities gain no weight at the dawn of the next epoch — the cost stays linear while influence stays flat.
